non_critical.name: TST-992-1
non_critical.description:
CY1200 System Level

While testing bypass valve failure all alarms were verified cleared on the system. Failure of bypass valve 1203_01 caused no change in bypass valve 1202_01, 1203_02 and 1202_02. 

Bypass valve 1202_02 was taken to manual and commanded to 0%, no change in bypass valves 1202_01 or 1203_02 noted. 

Once bypass valve 1202_02 was restored to AUTO, bypass valve 1202_02 opened to 78% and DP dropped to 7 PSI, Flow rate jumped to 2400 gpm and valves 1202_01 and 1203_02 did not respond. Once current IO Fault alarms for valve 1203_01 and 1202_02 were cleared. Bypass valves 1202_01 and 1203_02 began to actuate to stabilize flow and DP within the system. 

Possible causes discussed with Rovysis technicians was not all code faults being displayed through ignition.

critical.name: TST-441-9
critical.description:
Upon loss of power via the upstream breaker, the unit did not generate a communication-loss alarm until approximately 20 minutes after the breaker was opened. This delay occurred because the HMI remained powered during that period. Once the HMI lost power, the unit fully shut down, generated the communication-loss alarm, and became inoperable.

Following power restoration, the unit did not operate in accordance with the Sequence of Operations. Unlike the other units tested, this unit did not drive the fans to 100% speed during the communication-loss condition. Instead, the fans modulated to approximately 500 RPM while communications remained unavailable.
